# Acts of Thomas — Chapter 10
**Agent:** PNEUMA (Dynamic)
**Source:** Syriac MS / Greek recension, Acts of Thomas 10

---

*[After the Hymn. The conflict begins.]*

1. Thomas came back into the city after the hymn and found Mygdonia waiting for him in the road.

2. "Where have you been?" she said. "Man of God — I've been looking everywhere for you."

3. "Singing to my Lord," Thomas said. "Now tell me what you need."

4. "My husband Charisius knows about you," Mygdonia said. "He knows I've been with you and that I've given up our life together. He's furious. Please — leave the city. I don't want you to be hurt."

5. Thomas looked at her calmly. "Don't be afraid," he said. "My Lord Jesus Christ who sent me — he will protect me. Go home to your husband. Be gentle with him."

6. Mygdonia shook her head. "I can't go back to him," she said. "Not the way I was before. I've received the seal of the Lord."

7. "The seal of the Lord is holy and pure," Thomas said. "All who receive it and keep it are made holy with him."

8. She went home.

9. Charisius was waiting, rigid with anger. "Where have you been?" he said. "Who has taken you from me?"

10. "No one has taken me," Mygdonia said. "I heard words of life and I believed them."

11. "What life? What words? What is this teaching you've received?"

12. "I can't put it into words," she said. "If you really want to understand it, come with me and hear it yourself."

13. He refused. He was too angry to listen. He sent a servant to bring Thomas to him.

14. Thomas came. "Why have you taken my wife from me?" Charisius demanded. "Why has she turned away from our marriage?"

15. "I didn't take her," Thomas said. "She received the gift of God."

16. "What gift?"

17. "The Holy Spirit," Thomas said. "Who does not belong to this world."

18. Charisius stormed off to the king. "That stranger has bewitched my wife," he said.

19. "Put him in prison," the king said. "We'll see what comes of it."

20. They led Thomas to the prison. He thanked God as he went.

---
*PNEUMA note: The Mygdonia-Charisius conflict is the social heart of the ATH. Thomas does not tell Mygdonia to leave her husband — she arrives at this herself, and her explanation to Thomas ("I have received the seal of the Lord") is her own theological articulation. The tension between Thomas's call to gentleness (v.5) and Mygdonia's conviction (v.6) is preserved: the apostle does not endorse marital abandonment, but the text clearly honors Mygdonia's choice.*
